newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX MSCI Taiwan futures end weak in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX MSCI Taiwan futures end weak in dull trade.

text.p: SIMEX MSCI Taiwan index futures ended easier despite gains in the cash market on Wednesday, but interest continued to be hamstrung by tight trading ranges and low volumes.
Dealers said turnover was slightly better than it has been since the contract's launch on January 9, partly because the Nikkei futures market was closed for a Japanese holiday.
The March MSCI Taiwan stock index futures contract ended at 306.7 against its opening 306.0 after trading between 305.8 and 307.0. Volume was an estimated 624 lots.
The MSCI Taiwan index ended up 1.06 points at 314.42.
"We saw the cash moving but not the futures. It's such an illiquid market. It should be going higher with the cash market being bullish, but it isn't," said a trader.
Some dealers said it was difficult to chart the contract's expected trading levels due to a lack of historical data.

"SIMEX seems to be winning the volume battle over the CME. But if you look at the volumes more closely, most of it is coming from two locals trading on their own account," said a dealer with a European house.

He said the absence of Taiwanese retail customers, who appeared to be taking their authorities' warnings against trading the offshore contracts to heart, was severely dampening interest in the contract.
